faq.q: Can I ask for an as-is offer before rewiring the house?
faq.a: Yes. Share the known condition and available reports when requesting an evaluation. A proposal depends on the actual house and written terms; an as-is sale does not make an electrical hazard disappear.

faq.q: Does aluminum anywhere in the electrical system mean the same problem?
faq.a: No. The CPSC repair publication addresses particular aluminum branch-circuit wiring and distinguishes it from larger conductors and copper-clad aluminum. Have a qualified electrician identify the actual system.

faq.q: Does a new panel prove all aluminum wiring was repaired?
faq.a: No. A panel invoice describes only its stated scope. Ask whether the branch circuits, connections and other affected locations were evaluated or remediated.

faq.q: Should I open outlets or the panel to identify the wiring myself?
faq.a: No. This guide does not recommend opening electrical equipment. Arrange a qualified electrician's assessment and seek urgent help for active electrical danger.
